title: Anomalous Clues
next_chapter_hook: The Library Guardian Elder's cryptic reaction alerted Chen Ji; a barely perceptible flash of fear crossed that wrinkled face, as if Chen Ji had asked about something he shouldn't have.

text.content: Smoke slowly dissipated above the ruins of the Tianqing Sect, the残阳 crimson as blood, dyeing the devastated battlefield a desolate dark red. Among the broken walls and scattered ruins, the stench of blood mingled with the bitter scent of scorched earth, weighing heavily on every survivor's heart. Chen Ji stood alone at the edge of the purge's aftermath, his gray servant disciple robe stained with dust and blood, appearing particularly disheveled in the sunset. His gaze swept past the wreckage before him, landing on the nearby pile of looted spoils. The spoils formed a small mountain—weapons, artifacts, fragmented technique jade slips, and some miscellaneous items of unknown origin. On the surface, this was merely a routine post-battle inventory. Yet Chen Ji's brow center twitched slightly—his intuition told him that something within this pile of spoils should not be ignored.

He walked toward the spoils at a steady pace, his footsteps too composed for someone deemed worthless. Bending down, he began examining those weapons and jade slips one by one. His movements appeared casual, but each was precisely targeted. An ordinary disciple might only care about high-ranked artifacts, but Chen Ji was different—he was searching for things that 'shouldn't' be here. His fingertip traced a broken longsword, and his eyes sharpened. The blade's material was extremely rare, certainly not something an ordinary disciple could possess. Setting the broken sword aside, he continued searching. Suddenly, an ancient token slipped from the depths of the debris pile, 'ding'-ing against the ground and rolling to his feet.

Chen Ji bent to pick up the token, examining it closely in his palm. The token was barely the size of a palm, jet black as ink, yet surprisingly heavy in his hand. The surface's lacquer was mottled and worn, clearly quite old. However, what truly caught Chen Ji's attention was the symbol carved on the token's front—a vertical pupil, with an even smaller circle at its center, like some kind of诡异的符文. That symbol was eerily embedded deep into the token, as if branded with some special technique rather than ordinary carving. Chen Ji's pupils contracted sharply. He recognized this symbol.

On the cover of the Tianji Record, the same eye symbol was engraved. Except the Tianji Record's eye was golden, surrounded by intricate thunder patterns; this token's eye was dark crimson, appearing more sinister and subdued. The craftsmanship styles differed completely, yet the core symbol was identical. Chen Ji took a deep breath, forcing himself to remain calm. He flipped the token over—the back bore two nearly worn-away characters—'Tianji'. Though the strokes were fragmented, the character structure matched the title on the Tianji Record's cover. His heart skipped a beat. This token had a direct connection to the Tianji Record.

dialogue.content: "Chen Ji, what are you looking at?" Su Qingyao had somehow approached behind him. The Inner Disciple Senior Fellow's demeanor remained cold, but there was an inexplicable scrutiny in her gaze as she looked at Chen Ji. She had performed excellently in the purge, yet her face was still slightly pale from exhaustion. However, those eyes remained sharp, as if capable of seeing through all pretense. "There are things in the spoils worth noting." Chen Ji didn't hide it, handing the token over. He was clear that playing tricks before Su Qingyao would only backfire. Rather than conceal, it was better to display openly—after all, this token alone wasn't enough to expose the Tianji Record's existence.

text.content: Su Qingyao took the token, her slender fingers gently stroking the dark crimson eye symbol. Suddenly, her movements froze. "This pattern..." she murmured to herself, her brow creasing tightly, "I seem to have seen this somewhere." Chen Ji's heart tightened, though his expression remained unchanged. "What did Senior Sister Su recall?" Su Qingyao didn't answer immediately; instead, she brought the token close to her eyes, examining it carefully in the fading sunset. After a moment, she abruptly looked up, a flash of astonishment in her eyes. "This pattern matches the cover design of that forbidden book in the library... exactly."

The library's forbidden book? Chen Ji's pupils slightly contracted. Of course he knew the Tianqing Sect's scripture repository had several sealed texts involving ancient secrets, inaccessible to anyone below elder rank. But he had never imagined those forbidden books would be connected to the Tianji Record. Su Qingyao continued: "Deep within the library exists a secret chamber housing an ancient book without a name. That book's cover is covered with these eye symbols. I caught a glimpse of it once, and that image remains unforgettable." Her voice carried a hint of unease. "Those pupils... they seem alive. When they stare at you, it's as if they can pierce through your very soul."

Chen Ji fell silent for a moment, then tucked the token into his sleeve. That eye symbol also existed on the Tianji Record's cover, though normally concealed by golden thunder patterns—unnoticeable unless examined closely. The discovery of this token proved the Tianji Record was not unique—beyond it, other existences with eye symbols likely existed. What connection existed between these symbols? What faction or organization did they represent? More importantly, why had Mo Xiansheng never mentioned these? The remnant soul guardian was always elusive, appearing only when needed, yet always leaving words unsaid. An inexplicable restlessness surged in Chen Ji's heart—more mysteries multiplied, yet the clues he could control remained pitifully few.

Su Qingyao watched Chen Ji's token-stowing action, her expression thoughtful. "What do you intend to do with this matter?" Her tone was flat, yet carried a subtle probe. Chen Ji raised his head, meeting her gaze. Those eyes were deep as an abyss, seemingly harboring endless calculations, yet clear enough to hide their depths. "What does Senior Sister Su think?" He didn't answer directly, deflecting the question. Su Qingyao snorted lightly, seemingly dissatisfied with his evasiveness. But she didn't press further, merely remarking coolly: "Whatever you decide, I suggest you first investigate that forbidden book's origins. Some things, if pursued without clarification, may lead to consequences more severe than you can imagine."

Her warning was no exaggeration. Chen Ji understood clearly that in this world, power was the foundation of everything. With his current strength, he had no qualification to touch those deeper mysteries. But the question was—if he didn't investigate, he would forever remain in the dark, being led by those hidden manipulators. This passive, defensive situation was absolutely unacceptable to him. Chen Ji's gaze gradually sharpened; beneath that weak exterior, a cold heart was awakening anew. If Mo Xiansheng wouldn't tell him, he would investigate himself. The secrets of the Tianji Record, he would uncover with his own hands.

choice.prompt: Su Qingyao's warning echoed in Chen Ji's ears, and he had to make a choice. Immediate action, or careful planning?

choices.description: Without delay, proceed immediately to the scripture repository to investigate that forbidden book's origins. Though risks are high, delay only increases variables.
choices.visible_reward: Obtain crucial clues about the Tianji Record's origins
choices.risk_hint: The scripture repository's depths are heavily guarded; recklessly entering may startle the prey

text.content: Su Qingyao gave a slight nod, acknowledging Chen Ji's decision. "Since you've decided, I can take you to the scripture repository. However, the Library Guardian Elder is a troublesome character—you must be prepared mentally." Her tone carried a hint of worry, yet also a spark of anticipation.

choices.description: Temporarily suppress curiosity, secretly gather more intelligence before making plans. Haste makes waste; prudence takes precedence.
choices.visible_cost: May miss the optimal investigation window
choices.visible_reward: Maintain mystery, reduce exposure risk, buy more preparation time
choices.risk_hint: The token's aura may already have been detected by others; a long night invites many dreams

text.content: Su Qingyao's brow slightly furrowed, clearly disappointed by Chen Ji's cautious stance. "Very well, this matter indeed shouldn't be rushed." She returned the token to Chen Ji, her gaze flickering with complex emotions, seemingly reassessing this 'waste' of a junior brother.

Night deepens, stars sparse and few. The bell of Tianqing Sect rings softly, announcing the end of day's cultivation. Chen Ji stands in his modest Servants' Quarters, placing the ancient token on the table. Candlelight flickers, casting the dark red heterochromatic eye in shifting shadows, as if truly gazing at him. He extends his hand, fingertips gently touching the symbol. A faint warmth emanates from his fingertips—the Tianji Record Fragment trembles subtly within his body, as if some resonance has awakened between them. The sensation vanishes in an instant, yet Chen Ji has captured the crucial information—the connection between the token and the Tianji Record runs far deeper than he imagined.

Chen Ji withdraws his fingers, a thoughtful gleam flickering in his eyes. Mo Xiansheng remains silent in the depths of his consciousness, neither guiding nor obstructing, as if waiting for him to make his own decision. This very attitude speaks volumes—the secrets of the Tianji Record may be far more dangerous than he imagined. Mo Xiansheng is not testing him; he is protecting him. Choosing to investigate deeply means voluntarily stepping into an unknown maelstrom; choosing to remain still might mean missing the best opportunity to uncover the truth. Either choice carries immense risks and opportunities. Chen Ji's gaze shifts between the token and the window, finally settling in the direction of the Scripture Repository. There, the answers he needs lie hidden.

Suddenly, soft footsteps approach from outside the door. Chen Ji instantly suppresses his presence, hiding the token in his sleeve. The door is gently pushed open, and Su Qingyao's figure appears at the threshold. Moonlight spills from behind her, outlining her silhouette like a dream. "Haven't rest yet?" Her voice is soft, carrying a hint of undetectable concern. Chen Ji smiles faintly, that smile gentle as a spring breeze: "Isn't Senior Sister Su awake as well? Coming so late at night—something urgent?" Su Qingyao enters the room, her gaze lingering on him for a moment, seemingly searching for flaws. After a pause, she draws a yellowed paper from her sleeve and extends it before Chen Ji. "I found this while sorting through the Purge's spoils. Take a look yourself."

Chen Ji takes the paper, unfolds it—and his pupils constrict sharply. It is an incomplete map, seven positions marked in cinnabar, each bearing the same heterochromatic eye symbol. And in the map's center, four characters stand out prominently—"Tianji Returns." These four words make Chen Ji's heart sink heavily. Tianji Returns? What does it mean? Could it be that besides the Tianji Record Fragment in his possession, other parts are scattered across various places, and this token serves as some kind of key or token of authority? Su Qingyao's voice rings in his ears: "This map was found on a corpse I searched. The corpse's identity was unknown, but among the storage pouch were several tokens similar to yours."

The fingers holding the paper tighten slightly, producing a soft crinkling sound. Chen Ji forces himself to remain calm, memorizing every detail on the paper. Then, before Su Qingyao's eyes, he brings the paper to the candle flame and ignites it. Fire devours those mysterious symbols; Chen Ji's expression alternates between light and shadow in the firelight. "You're not going to let me see it?" Su Qingyao's voice carries a hint of displeasure. Chen Ji shakes his head: "Senior Sister Su, some things—the less one knows, the safer." His tone is uncommonly serious, "This matter runs too deep. I don't want to involve you in unnecessary trouble." Su Qingyao stares at him for a long while, then suddenly laughs softly: "Chen Ji, are you truly just a Servant Disciple?"

dialogue.content: This question strikes Chen Ji's soft underbelly like a sharp blade. He knows Su Qingyao is drawing ever closer to the truth. This woman is too perceptive—every time he believes his disguise is airtight, flaws surface before her. But he cannot admit it, not at least for now. Chen Ji reveals a bitter smile: "Senior Sister Su jokes. If I were someone remarkable, how could I have wasted so many years in the Servants' Hall?" His performance is flawless, the tone carrying just the right amount of self-mockery and helplessness. Su Qingyao gazes at him, seemingly trying to find flaws in his eyes. But finally, she merely sighs softly: "Very well, if you won't speak, I won't force you. Just remember—if you need anything, you can come to me." She turns and leaves, her footsteps gradually fading into the night.

text.content: Chen Ji closes the door, leans against it, and exhales a long breath. Su Qingyao's intuition is terrifyingly sharp—he must be even more careful. However, the map she brought does provide crucial clues. "Tianji Returns"—these four characters echo endlessly in his mind. What does it mean? Was the Tianji Record once complete, later deliberately split apart? Or is this part of some grander design? Regardless, investigating the Scripture Repository has become imperative. That forbidden book sealed away with the same heterochromatic eye symbol may hold the truth of the Tianji Record's origins.

choice.prompt: After Su Qingyao left, Chen Ji needed to decide his next move. Investigate the Scripture Repository tonight, or wait until the timing was more mature?

choices.description: Su Qingyao's appearance made the situation more urgent—those token owners numbered more than one. He must investigate the Scripture Repository before anyone else.
choices.visible_cost: Night action carries greater risks; it may alert the Scripture Repository's elder.
choices.visible_reward: Seize the initiative and obtain firsthand intelligence.
choices.risk_hint: Night patrols are even more stringent—once exposed, one would be in an extremely passive position.

text.content: Chen Ji changes into dark night attire, tucking the token and map securely against his body. He pushes open the window, his figure flashing once, then vanishes into the night. The outline of the Scripture Repository looms indistinct beneath the moonlight, like a dormant beast, waiting for prey to walk into its trap. And he is the one prepared to pry open the beast's fangs.

choices.description: Night action is too risky—better to wait until tomorrow daytime, then enter the Scripture Repository openly under the pretense of sorting through spoils.
choices.visible_cost: Requires spending a day arranging things; may miss critical clues.
choices.visible_reward: More稳妥, reduces the risk of exposure.
choices.risk_hint: The longer the delay, the more variables arise.

text.content: Chen Ji closes the window again, sitting back at the table. Tonight is not suitable for action—he needs more time to deduce every possibility. The candle on the table reignites, stretching his shadow long and long. He closes his eyes, fingers tapping lightly on the table's surface, countless thoughts colliding within his mind. Tomorrow, everything will be decided.

Regardless of the choice, one thing is certain—that ancient token carved with the heterochromatic eye symbol did not appear among the spoils by chance. Its appearance, like a stone cast into a lake, will inevitably stir rippling waves. Chen Ji grips the token in his palm, feeling that faint, intangible warmth. The secrets of the Tianji Record, Mo Xiansheng's true identity, and the true meaning of "Tianji Returns" on that map... All the riddles point in the same direction. And that direction is the fate he is destined to be unable to escape. Outside the window, moonlight flows like water, scattering over every corner of Tianqing Sect. The distant Scripture Repository stands silently in the night, like a dormant beast awaiting the coming storm.

Chen Ji finally makes his decision—he chooses to wait for dawn. Not because he is cowardly, but because he needs more preparation. Mo Xiansheng remains silent, yet that silence itself is a form of permission. Chen Ji retrieves the Tianji Record Fragment, examining those golden patterns once more under the moonlight. He discovers, in a corner of the fragment, a line of extremely faint small characters he had never noticed before. "Heavenly Secrets Pavilion opens; seven lineages merge as one." These eight characters are like a prophecy, like a guide, echoing "Tianji Returns" on the map Su Qingyao brought. Heavenly Secrets Pavilion? Seven lineages merge as one? Could it be that the complete form of the Tianji Record is hidden in a place called the "Heavenly Secrets Pavilion"?

Chen Ji's heart quickens. If his speculation is correct, not only does the complete version of the Tianji Record exist, it is likely sealed away in some secret location. Those seven positions marked with the heterochromatic eye symbol may be the seven paths leading to the Heavenly Secrets Pavilion. And the token in his hand, that fragment, and the map Su Qingyao discovered—all are keys to opening this gate. The mysteries begin to clarify, but the dangers multiply correspondingly. The existence capable of arranging such a grand chess game is no ordinary person. Ling Yuan, Ye Qing, even the mysterious Scripture Repository's elder... Each person may play a different role in this game.

Chen Ji closes the fragment, returning it within his body. Moonlight spills through the window lattice, casting mottled shadows across his face. His expression remains calm as usual, but within his eyes burns a light never seen before. This game—he has played it for too long. From the moment he transmigrated to this world, he has been fumbling, struggling, enduring within the game. The waste persona was his best protective color, allowing him to accumulate strength in the shadows, waiting for the moment to astonish the world. Now, that moment is finally coming. He will not let anyone obstruct his path, even if that enemy is Heaven itself.

Night deepens further; the commotion of Tianqing Sect has completely subsided. Chen Ji lies on the bed but has no intention of closing his eyes. Within his mind, he continuously deduces every move for tomorrow—how to enter the Scripture Repository, how to approach that forbidden book, how to find the clues he needs beneath the watchful eyes of the Scripture Repository's elder. Su Qingyao's appearance is a double-edged sword—she is both an asset and a threat. This woman is far too clever; the slightest carelessness will let him see through more. But he cannot push her away, not at least for now. Before completely uncovering the truth, he needs more pieces that can be utilized. The night stretches on silently, carrying forward all the unresolved mysteries.

Just as Chen Ji was about to fall asleep, the fragment of the Tianji Record suddenly grew slightly warm. This strange phenomenon startled him awake, and he sat up to carefully sense what was happening. That warmth surged from deep within the fragment, like some long-dormant power being awakened. Then, an aged voice rang out in his mind—that was Mo Xiansheng's voice. "You found it." The guardian of the residual soul's tone carried a complex meaning. "That token is one of the keys to the Tianji Pavilion. But do not use it lightly until you are prepared." This was the first time Mo Xiansheng had proactively mentioned the existence of the Tianji Pavilion. Chen Ji wanted to ask for more, but Mo Xiansheng had already fallen silent again, as if everything just now had merely been an illusion.

Chen Ji clenched his fist, his knuckles turning white from the force. Mo Xiansheng's warning made him even more certain that the existence of the Tianji Pavilion was far more dangerous than he had imagined. What secrets was that place hiding? And was he truly "prepared"? The night deepened, and Chen Ji lay on his简陋 bed, gazing at the mottled ceiling above. The secrets of the Tianji Record, the mystery of the异瞳 symbol, the prophecy of the Seven Pulses returning to their places... all the clues pointed in the same direction. He knew that from the moment he picked up that token, there was no turning back. The moon beyond the window gradually sank westward, and a glimmer of dawn began to appear in the eastern sky. Dawn was coming.

The morning bell of the Tianqing Sect rang悠悠, announcing the arrival of a new day. Chen Ji opened his eyes, his gaze showing no trace of drowsiness—he had stayed awake all night, yet felt spirited. Pushing open the door, the chill of early morning rushed to meet him, instantly clearing his mind. In the distance, the Scripture Repository glowed with an ancient luster under the morning sun, its flying eaves and bucket arches appearing solemn and dignified in the dawn light. Chen Ji took a deep breath, straightened his clothes, and walked toward that direction. His footsteps seemed casual, but in truth, every step was precisely calculated. Today, he would enter that forbidden place openly, in the guise of a servant disciple. The Law Enforcement Elder's深不可测 expression made alarm bells ring in his heart—the old man must surely be hiding some unspeakable secret.
